prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case, how severe the injuries are, and what kind of lawyer you want (big-firm trial shop vs. smaller boutique that handles just truck/auto cases). I can help you find the best fit, but here are practical steps and criteria to use right away plus where to look and what to ask.

Immediate things to know and do
- Texas statute of limitations for personal injury: 2 years from the date of the crash (so act promptly).  
- Get and keep medical records, police/crash report, photos, witness names/contacts, insurance info, repair bills, wage-loss documentation.  
- Preserve evidence (phone records, truck dashcam/ELD data if possible). Truck cases often require quick preservation of carrier logs and ELD data.

Where to find good truck-accident attorneys
- State and local resources: Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral, Texas State Bar directory.  
- Independent rating sites: Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Best Lawyers (look for AV or peer-review ratings).  
- Professional organizations: Texas Trial Lawyers Association, American Association for Justice (AAJ) — members often handle serious injury cases and have trial experience.  
- Local courtroom reputation and recent verdicts/settlements — check news articles and firm press releases.

Key criteria to evaluate
- Specific truck-accident experience (not just general car-crash work). Truck cases involve federal regs, carrier liability, ELDs, logbooks, and specialized experts.  
- Trial experience and verdict history — many big insurers only take settlements seriously if you will actually litigate.  
- Resources and staffing — can the firm hire accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and investigators?  
- Communication and availability — responsiveness matters.  
- Fee structure — most work on contingency (commonly ~33% for pre-suit; may increase if suit/filed). Confirm costs/advance expenses policy.  
- Disciplinary history — check Texas Bar for any sanctions.

Questions to ask any prospective lawyer
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases against the same carrier/insurance company involved in my crash?  
- What results have you obtained for clients with injuries like mine?  
- Who in your office will handle my case day-to-day? How often will I get updates?  
- What is your fee and how are expenses handled?  
- What is your strategy and timeline for my case?

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short list of well-rated Dallas attorneys/firms that specialize in truck accidents (I’ll pull contact info, peer ratings, and recent verdicts/settlements).  
- Draft an email or list of questions to send to attorneys.  
- Help evaluate retainer agreements or settlement offers (I can’t give legal advice, but I can help you understand terms).

Tell me: are you in Dallas now? When was the crash and how serious are the injuries? Do you prefer a large firm or a smaller boutique, and do you want me to compile a shortlist of attorneys for you?
